headline: Thanksgiving and Friday are sunny, dry and very warm, with Friday the warmest day at 12 to 15 degrees above normal and gusty northeast winds in the mountains, while a big swell and exceptionally high tides flood parts of the coast this morning; models agree strongly on a moderate to strong storm Tuesday–Wednesday that could bring 1–3 inches of rain to the coasts and valleys.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Thanksgiving is sunny and very warm around Glendale and the rest of LA, with dry winds blowing out from the interior (offshore winds) at their strongest today. Highs reach the upper 70s to mid 80s across the coasts and valleys south of Point Conception and the mid 70s to lower 80s farther north, with skies mostly clear apart from some possible high clouds. Gusts should reach low-end advisory levels in the Santa Lucia Mountains, Santa Susana Mountains and western San Gabriel Mountains, with a Wind Advisory from 6 AM to 2 PM today and another running until 9 AM Friday, while other wind-prone spots stay just below advisory levels. Light turbulence and wind shear are possible near Burbank, Van Nuys and Camarillo until about 9 AM.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Winds ease a little Friday, but Friday is the warmest day, 1 to 3 degrees warmer than Thanksgiving with highs 12 to 15 degrees above normal. On Saturday the offshore winds are noticeably weaker and an ocean breeze may return in the afternoon, cooling things off 4 to 8 degrees, though highs stay above normal. It stays dry through Saturday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Sunday brings increasing clouds and 3 to 6 degrees of cooling, with rain chances on the Central Coast in the afternoon and rain likely there Sunday evening, while the LA area stays dry; Sunday night brings a 20 to 30 percent chance of light rain south of Point Conception, with Central Coast totals under a quarter inch and more likely under a tenth. Monday is cloudy with a 30 to 40 percent chance of rain at any time of day, a quarter to a third of an inch possible (most on the coast-facing mountain slopes and Central Coast), and highs near normal. Then a cold storm system is expected to drop in from the north Tuesday or Tuesday night, with the heaviest rain Tuesday tapering off Wednesday: 1 to 3 inches for the coasts and valleys, 3 to 5 inches on coast-facing slopes and half an inch to 1.5 inches in the far interior, plus a chance of thunderstorms if the storm center passes overhead. Snow should only stick above about 7,500 feet, and highs will mostly be in the 60s Tuesday and Wednesday.

coast: A large, long-period west swell peaks this morning and combines with exceptionally high tides to bring large surf and moderate to significant coastal flooding, worst at the morning high tide and in low-lying spots with no protection from the ocean. The biggest surf and worst flooding are on the Central Coast from Point Conception northward, the Ventura County coast and far eastern parts of the southern Santa Barbara County coast, under Coastal Flood Warnings until noon today and High Surf Warnings ending this morning, followed by High Surf Advisories lasting into Saturday (until noon or 9 PM Saturday depending on the stretch of coast); other beaches see somewhat lesser but still concerning impacts under Coastal Flood Advisories until noon today and High Surf Advisories until noon or 9 PM today. Expect strong rip currents nearly everywhere, strong along-shore currents, sneaker waves, heavy shore break, coastal erosion and a higher risk of damage to coastal structures, making swimming dangerous. On the water, large breaking waves near the coast and harbor entrances can capsize small boats through today; Small Craft Advisories run until 3 PM today for some waters and until 3 AM Friday for others, with offshore advisory-strength winds from Point Mugu to Santa Monica into tonight and rough seas on the outer waters and north of Point Sal through Friday. Conditions are mostly calmer Friday night through Monday, then winds increase to advisory levels or higher Monday night ahead of the strong midweek storm.
watch_for: Coastal flooding and dangerous surf at this morning's high tide, worst on the Central Coast and Ventura County coast
Gusty northeast winds in the Santa Susana, western San Gabriel and Santa Lucia Mountains today into Friday morning
The Tuesday–Wednesday storm: 1–3 inches of rain for the coasts and valleys and 3–5 inches on the slopes, with timing that could shift by about 12 hours
confidence: Forecasters show no notable doubt about the warm, dry stretch through Saturday, say there is remarkable agreement among all forecast models on a moderate to strong storm Tuesday–Wednesday though its timing could shift by about 12 hours, and have moderate to high confidence in the marine forecast.
